title: EmTech Future 2026: When AI Meets Everything

# EmTech Future 2026: When AI Meets Everything

Plus a special MIT Technology Review Insiders Panel

Only available to MIT Technology Review subscribers.

Yossi Matias, Vice President & Head of Google Research, explores how AI is beginning to reshape biology, infrastructure, manufacturing, and science, and why its greatest impact may come when it intersects with other fields.

Step inside the newsroom with our MIT Technology Review editors for sharp analysis and unpublished insights from the team that researches and reports on emerging tech daily.

## There’s much more to discover

These are just two sessions from EmTech Future 2026.

Across three days, EmTech Future explored some of the most important questions shaping technology right now: how AI is impacting industries, where quantum is heading, what new energy systems could make possible, how robotics are evolving, and what challenges and opportunities arise when these technologies start to converge.

Hear the ideas, insights, and perspectives you missed at EmTech Future 2026.

The full program is now available on demand, giving you access to all the conversations and sessions from the event, including:

* Quantum in context Hartmut Neven, founder and lead at Google Quantum AI, explores how quantum is advancing alongside other frontiers and why its significance may lie not only in what it can do on its own, but in how it begins to interact with the systems around it.

* Energy Systems for the Future Evelyn Wang, VP for energy & climate at MIT, explores how energy, computing, infrastructure, and climate technologies are increasingly interconnected, and what these converging systems could mean for the future of industry and society.

* Rethinking our relationship with AI –Cory Doctorow, bestselling author and award-winning writer, explores how AI is changing the way we work and think.

As an MIT Technology Review subscriber, you’ll get a 20% discount, meaning you can access the full EmTech Future 2026 program for just $596.
